name: ChatGPT
blurb: General-purpose AI assistant that can brainstorm game ideas, write and debug code, and draft dialogue or design docs.
age_note: OpenAI terms: 13+; users under 18 need a parent or guardian's permission.

name: Claude
blurb: AI assistant strong at long code files; its Artifacts feature can produce small playable browser games from a prompt.
age_note: Anthropic requires Claude users to be 18+.

name: Grok
blurb: xAI's assistant for brainstorming, coding help and quick prototype generation.
age_note: xAI terms: 13+; ages 13–17 need parental permission.

name: Gemini
blurb: Google's multimodal assistant; Canvas mode can build and preview simple web games.
age_note: Needs a Google account; teen access and minimum ages vary by country.

name: Claude Code
blurb: Agentic coding tool in your terminal that edits whole game projects, runs builds and fixes errors.
note: Included with paid Claude plans (Pro $20/mo or $17/mo billed annually, Max, Team, Enterprise) or usable with API credits; not on the free plan.
age_note: Requires a Claude account (18+).

name: OpenAI Codex
blurb: OpenAI's coding agent for writing, refactoring and testing game code across a repository.
note: Included across ChatGPT plans, with limited access on Free and Go; Plus is $20/mo.
age_note: Uses a ChatGPT account (13+, under-18s need parental permission).

name: Cursor
blurb: AI-first code editor popular for 'vibe coding' games in Godot, Unity or JavaScript.
age_note: Cursor terms: 18+ (or local age of majority).

name: GitHub Copilot
blurb: AI pair programmer inside VS Code and other editors for game scripting.
age_note: GitHub accounts require age 13+.

name: Meshy
blurb: Generates textured 3D models from text or images, handy for placeholder or stylized game assets.
age_note: Meshy terms: 14+; under-18s need parental permission.

name: Tripo
blurb: Text- and image-to-3D model generator with export to common game formats.
age_note: Check Tripo's terms for the current minimum age.

name: Suno
blurb: Creates full songs from text prompts; check the plan terms before using tracks commercially.
age_note: Check Suno's terms for the current minimum age.

name: ElevenLabs
blurb: AI voice generation and sound effects for character dialogue and prototypes.
age_note: ElevenLabs terms: 18+ (or local age of majority).

name: Scenario
blurb: AI image generation tuned for consistent game art styles and asset sets.
age_note: Professional tool; check Scenario's terms for the minimum age.

name: Godot Engine
blurb: Free, MIT-licensed 2D/3D engine with a lightweight editor and Python-like GDScript.
age_note: No account needed. Motivated younger kids can start with an adult's help.

name: Unity
blurb: Widely used C# engine for mobile, PC, console and XR games, with a huge asset store.
note: Unity Personal is free if revenue + funding ≤ US$200K (prior 12 months); Unity Pro is required above that (US$2,310/seat/yr). The Runtime Fee was cancelled in Sept 2024; no royalties.
age_note: Publishing to stores is subject to each store's age rules.

name: Unreal Engine
blurb: High-end 3D engine with Blueprints visual scripting and C++. Free to start; games pay a 5% royalty only on lifetime gross revenue above US$1M per product.
note: Epic Games Store revenue is royalty-exempt. Non-game commercial users with >US$1M annual revenue need seats at US$1,850/yr.
age_note: Requires an Epic Games account; demanding hardware.

name: GameMaker
blurb: Classic 2D engine behind many indie hits, free for non-commercial use.
note: Free for non-commercial use; Professional is a one-time US$99.99 to sell games; console export needs Enterprise (US$79.99/mo or US$799.99/yr).
age_note: Account required; selling games needs a paid license.

name: Defold
blurb: Free, lightweight Lua engine great for small, fast mobile and web games.

name: Bevy
blurb: Data-driven open-source game engine written in Rust using an ECS architecture.
age_note: Advanced Rust programming.

name: Phaser
blurb: Popular open-source JavaScript framework for 2D browser games.

name: PICO-8
blurb: A 'fantasy console' with built-in code, sprite, map and music editors and tight, charming limits.
age_note: Simple Lua coding; curious older kids often enjoy it with help.

name: Roblox Studio
blurb: Free tool to build and publish Roblox experiences in Luau, with built-in monetization.
age_note: Anyone with a Roblox account can build. Publishing for under-16 audiences requires a verified, age-checked creator account with 2-step verification; payments for 13–17s need parental consent.

name: UEFN (Unreal Editor for Fortnite)
blurb: Build and publish Fortnite islands with Unreal tools and the Verse language.
age_note: Building is open to Fortnite players, but publishing through the Fortnite Developer Program requires a legal adult.

name: Construct 3
blurb: Browser-based no-code 2D engine using event sheets.
note: Free tier is limited (50 events, 2 layers, web export); personal subscription is about US$129.99/yr.
age_note: Runs in the browser; widely used in schools.

name: GDevelop
blurb: Open-source no-code engine for 2D and 3D games, with one-click export.
note: Editor and engine are MIT-licensed and free; optional subscriptions add cloud builds, AI credits and online services.
age_note: No-code events; friendly for younger makers with guidance.

name: RPG Maker MZ
blurb: Make classic-style JRPGs with map, database and event editors.

name: Bitsy
blurb: Tiny browser editor for small pixel-art narrative games.
age_note: No account needed; runs in the browser.

name: Twine
blurb: Open-source tool for interactive, nonlinear text stories.
age_note: No account needed; great for writers of any age.

name: Ren'Py
blurb: Free, open-source visual novel engine (free for commercial use) that exports to desktop, mobile and web.

name: LÖVE
blurb: Minimal open-source Lua framework for 2D games.

name: MonoGame
blurb: Open-source C# framework, the spiritual successor to XNA.
age_note: Advanced C# programming.

name: Stride
blurb: Open-source C# 3D engine with a full editor.
age_note: Advanced C# programming.

name: Blender
blurb: Free, open-source 3D suite for modeling, rigging, animation and texturing game assets.
age_note: Free, no account; steep but rewarding learning curve.

name: Aseprite
blurb: Beloved pixel-art and sprite animation editor; source is available to compile yourself.
note: One-time purchase (US$19.99 on the official site/Steam).

name: Krita
blurb: Free, open-source digital painting app for concept art and 2D assets.
age_note: Free, no account needed.

name: MagicaVoxel
blurb: Free voxel art editor and renderer for blocky 3D models.
age_note: Free, no account needed.

name: Adobe Substance 3D Painter
blurb: Industry-standard 3D texture painting for PBR game assets.
age_note: Professional, paid tool.

name: Tiled
blurb: Free, flexible tile map editor supported by many engines.

name: LDtk
blurb: Modern open-source 2D level editor from the director of Dead Cells.

name: Kenney Assets
blurb: Thousands of free, public-domain (CC0) game assets for prototypes and releases.
age_note: Free CC0 assets; no account needed.

name: Audacity
blurb: Free audio editor for recording and cleaning up sound effects and voice.

name: LMMS
blurb: Open-source music production app for game soundtracks.

name: Bfxr / jsfxr
blurb: Generate retro sound effects (jumps, coins, explosions) in one click.
age_note: One-click sound effects in the browser.

name: FMOD
blurb: Adaptive audio middleware integrated with Unity and Unreal; free for small indies.
age_note: Professional audio middleware.

name: Bosca Ceoil Blue
blurb: Open-source remake of the classic Bosca Ceoil — a simple music maker loved for game jam soundtracks.
age_note: Simple, free music maker.

name: Scratch
blurb: Free block-based coding from MIT where kids make and share games and stories.
age_note: Designed for ages 8–16; anyone can use it. Children under 13 need a parent's email to register.

name: Minecraft Education
blurb: Classroom edition of Minecraft with coding lessons via MakeCode and Python.
age_note: Provided through schools and education licenses.

name: Microsoft MakeCode Arcade
blurb: Free block-and-JavaScript editor for retro arcade games in the browser.
age_note: Free, runs in the browser; no account needed to start.

name: Dreams
blurb: PS4 creation game for sculpting, animating and scripting games; live support ended in 2023.
age_note: Rated ESRB T / PEGI 12. PS4 game; live support ended in 2023.

name: Super Mario Maker 2
blurb: Design and share Mario levels — a fun intro to level design.
age_note: Rated ESRB E. Sharing levels online needs Nintendo Switch Online.

name: Game Builder Garage
blurb: Nintendo's guided visual programming game that teaches game logic step by step.
age_note: Rated ESRB E.

name: Core
blurb: Unreal-powered free platform for creating and publishing multiplayer games.

name: Meta Horizon Worlds Desktop Editor
blurb: Build social VR worlds for Meta Horizon with TypeScript and desktop tools.
note: Early access; runs via the Meta Quest Link PC app.
age_note: Requires a Meta account; check Meta's current age rules for creators.

name: Meta XR SDK (Unity)
blurb: Official SDKs for building Quest VR/MR games in Unity or Unreal.
age_note: Developer tools; Quest headsets are designed for ages 10+ with parent-managed accounts.

name: ShapesXR
blurb: Prototype and storyboard VR/AR scenes collaboratively inside a headset.
age_note: Professional design tool.

name: itch.io
blurb: Open indie storefront: upload games free, set your own revenue share, join game jams.
age_note: itch.io: users 13+; publishers must be 18+ or have parental or guardian consent.

name: Steamworks
blurb: Publish on Steam for a US$100 Steam Direct fee per game, recouped once the game earns US$1,000 in adjusted gross revenue.
age_note: Requires identity, tax and banking details; minors typically need a parent, guardian or company.

name: Google Play Console
blurb: Publish Android games for a one-time US$25 developer registration fee.
age_note: Developer registration requires an adult (18+).

name: Apple App Store
blurb: Ship iOS games via the Apple Developer Program (US$99 per membership year).
age_note: Apple Developer Program members must be of legal age (age of majority).

name: GitHub Pages
blurb: Free static hosting — perfect for HTML5 games and jam builds.
age_note: GitHub accounts require age 13+.

name: Newgrounds
blurb: Long-running community portal for browser games and animation.
age_note: Hosts mature content; 13+.

name: GDQuest
blurb: Godot tutorials and courses, including free interactive GDScript lessons.

name: Unity Learn
blurb: Free official Unity pathways from first project to job-ready.

name: Brackeys
blurb: Famous YouTube channel for friendly Unity and Godot tutorials.
age_note: YouTube channel; YouTube accounts are 13+.

name: Game Programming Patterns
blurb: Free online book explaining design patterns for game code.

name: Global Game Jam
blurb: Annual worldwide jam — make a game in 48 hours with others.
age_note: Local jam sites set their own age rules.

name: CS50's Intro to Game Development
blurb: Free Harvard course building classic games in LÖVE and Unity.
